note: Anchors are the grader's regression suite. An anchor is a site plus the band a human says it belongs in. Offline anchors are HTML fixtures and run in CI; live anchors are real URLs and only run with --live because they change under us. Change a weight, run grade-calibrate.js, and these tell you whether you improved the grader or just moved it.

gates.note: Offline anchors must land in the exact expected band, every time; they are fixtures and there is no excuse for drift. Live anchors are allowed to miss one in five because real sites change.

anchors.why: Everything a small-business site should be: schema, tap-to-call, hours, form, responsive imagery, real copy. If this ever drops out of the excellent band, the weights are broken.
A 2019 Bootstrap site: works, responsive, but fixed-width container, no schema, no tel: link, thin copy. This is the refresh lane and it must not read as either excellent or broken.
Table layout, font tags, marquee, jQuery 1.7, no viewport, copyright 2011. The obsolescence ceiling has to bite here, because the page loads fast for exactly the reason it is worthless.

anchors.source: Mac, Slack DM 2026-08-05: named Suraya as the example of a prospect that already has a good website
anchors.why: The anchor that started the project. Mac's judgment, encoded. If the grader ever routes Suraya into a website pitch, the grader is wrong.

anchors.source: Same batch as Suraya; James Beard award restaurant on a professionally built Squarespace site
anchors.why: Client-rendered. Catches the failure mode where static HTML looks empty and a good site scores like a broken one.
Proof the problem is not only restaurants. An agency-built home-services site with 12k words and Plumber schema does not need us, and B3/B4 are full of these.
No website at all, only a trade-union contractor listing. Must never be graded as a bad site; must route on the no-site path. With review data on the row this becomes the build lane.
